newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Gunmen kill politician, five others in Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill politician, five others in Sri Lanka.

text.p: Gunmen killed an opposition parliamentarian and five other people, including a four-year-old boy, near Sri Lanka's eastern town of Trincomalee on Sunday, police said.
They said United National Party (UNP) deputy Mohammed Moharoof's jeep was ambushed between Trincomalee and the nearby beach resort of Nilaveli at about 10.30 a.m. (0430 GMT).
The other victims were Moharoof's driver, his bodyguard, a colleague, a principal of a local Moslem school and the driver's four-year-old son, police said.
Police blamed separatist guerrillas of the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) for the killings.
"We are still making inquiries," a police officer said. No arrests had been made so far, he added.
Police said three groups of rebels opened fire at Moharoof's jeep and pumped 20 bullets into him. Seventy-eight bullet marks were found on his vehicle.
The LTTE are fighting a 13-year-old war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE puts the toll higher.
Police said Moharoof was travelling in the Moslem-dominated area around Trincomalee, visiting villages where LTTE rebels had kidnapped fishermen in recent weeks.
They said the lawmaker had met local police to discuss the villagers' safety just before he was killed.
Moharoof, 58, was a deputy minister in the UNP government which lost power to the ruling People's Alliance in 1994.
Political parties in Sri Lanka condemned Moharoof's killing and security has been tightened in Trincomalee, where his remains will be buried early on Monday.
Moharoof was the second parliamentary deputy to be killed this month in Trincomalee, 260 km (160 miles) northeast of Colombo.
Arunasalam Thangathurai, Trincomalee parliamentary deputy for the Tamil United Liberation Front (TULF), died in a grenade attack on July 5.
Police blamed the LTTE for Thangathurai's killing, but nobody has claimed responsibility for the murder.
